Medical : hydroxyurea first line; definitive : splenectomy
Medical : interferon; definitive : no curative option listed

units.title: Overview: CMP Physiology, MPN Pathology and the Printed MPN List with Mutations
units.sec: Overview: CMP Physiology, MPN Pathology and the Printed MPN List with Mutations
units.guide:
Physiology diagram: CMP → terminal myeloid cells (RBC, platelets, monocytes, eosinophils, basophils); pathology = proliferation of mature cells of multiple lineages with no dysplastic/immature cells.
MPN list: 1 PCRV (m/c), 2 PMF, 3 ET — bracketed under JAK-2 (PMF additionally deletion on chr 9p); 4 CML = BCR-ABL t(9;22); 5 CNL = CSF3R; 6 CEL = PDGFRA; 7 JMML and 8 MPN-NOS are BCR-ABL negative.
Notes: 1° myelofibrosis (myelophthisis) = bone marrow failure; systemic mastocytosis (c-kit) is excluded from MPN.

units.title: Clinical Features of MPN, Polycythemia Thresholds and Relative Polycythemia (Gaisböck's)
units.sec: Clinical Features of MPN, Polycythemia Thresholds and Relative Polycythemia (Gaisböck's)
units.guide:
EMH at spleen (m/c), skin, liver; splenomegaly massive in CML/PMF, moderate in PCRV, mild in ET; classical B symptoms in 20%; MPN can transform into each other or AML; MDS = ineffective proliferation → pancytopenia; MDS/MPN overlap in WHO 5th edition.
Polycythemia table: male Hb ≥16.5 gm%/PCV 49, female ≥16/48; types relative and absolute.
Relative polycythemia (Gaisböck's): ↓ plasma volume (dehydration) → ↑ Hb%, post-viral; investigations show normal RBC mass/TC/PLC with ↑ Hb.

units.title: Absolute Polycythemia: Types, EPO/TC/PLC Table and Secondary Etiologies
units.sec: Absolute Polycythemia: Types, EPO/TC/PLC Table and Secondary Etiologies
units.guide:
Absolute = increased RBC mass; primary (PCRV) vs secondary; table: EPO normal-to-low in PCRV vs increased in secondary; TC/PLC increased in PCRV vs normal in secondary.
EPO = erythropoietin (cortex and outer medulla of kidney); hypoxic causes: COPD, OSAS, high altitude, CO intoxication, hepatopulmonary syndrome; renal artery stenosis separate.
Paraneoplastic: renal carcinoma (hypernephroma), cerebellar hemangioblastoma (von Hippel-Lindau), meningioma, pheochromocytoma (pallor ⇒ malignancy), hepatoma, uterine fibroids; features headache, dizziness, hypertension in paraneoplastic patients.

units.title: Polycythemia Rubra Vera: JAK2 Mutations and Clinical Features
units.sec: Polycythemia Rubra Vera: JAK2 Mutations and Clinical Features
units.guide:
PCRV = m/c MPN, age 50–60, female > male; JAK-2 in 100% (exon 14 V617F 95%, exon 12 5%).
Erythrocytosis: hyperviscosity, thrombosis arterial > venous (arterial stroke in young; venous Budd-Chiari/DVT; microvascular erythromelalgia), hypertension.
Granulocytosis: neutrophilia, basophilia → histamine → aquagenic pruritus, ↑ transcobalamin-I → ↑ B12 binding capacity; thrombocytosis → dysfunctional platelets → bleeding (epistaxis, acquired vWD); moderate splenomegaly; hyperuricemia (↑ turnover).
Investigations: ↑ RBC with ↓ MCV/normal MCH, low ESR (↓ rouleaux), PS microcytosis with erythrocytosis, LAP high, ↑ B12 binding capacity.

units.title: PCRV Investigations, Diagnostic Criteria and Management; Primary Myelofibrosis Etiology
units.sec: PCRV Investigations, Diagnostic Criteria and Management; Primary Myelofibrosis Etiology
units.guide:
Note: ↓ MCV (to conserve MCH) → no rouleaux; microcytosis list hypoxia, thalassemia, PCRV; transcobalamin from neutrophils for transport (liver, etc.).
Criteria: major Hb >16.5 men/>16 women, marrow hypercellularity, JAK-2; minor subnormal serum EPO.
Management: low risk <60 yrs — phlebotomy weekly (Hb 13–14) + aspirin; high risk >60 yrs/h/o thrombosis — phlebotomy + aspirin 75 mg + ruxolitinib 10 mg BD (or) hydroxyurea 0.5–2 g/day.
PMF etiology: JAK-2 50%, CALR 30–40%, MPL (codes for thrombopoietin) 10–20%, triple negative = poor prognosis, deletion 13q.

units.title: Primary Myelofibrosis: Pathogenesis and Clinical Features
units.sec: Primary Myelofibrosis: Pathogenesis and Clinical Features
units.guide:
Dysplastic megakaryocytes (lack CXCR4) in hypercellular marrow release TGF-β (most potent fibrogenic cytokine) and PDGF → marrow fibrosis (↑ type-III collagen); premature-cell release → leukoerythroblastosis and pancytopenia.
Most present in fibrotic stage; age >60; male = female; thrombosis risk PCRV > ET > PMF; B symptoms 20%; fatigue (m/c) from anemia; gout in proliferation stage.
EMH: massive splenomegaly (75%), osteosclerosis, hepatomegaly (portal hypertension), skin febrile neutrophilic dermatosis (Sweet syndrome — note: characteristic of AML); cutaneous photos show annular lesions (A,B,D), erythematous lower-limb lesions, erythematous papules and plaques.

units.title: Primary Myelofibrosis: Investigations and Management
units.guide:
PS: anisopoikilocytosis with teardrop cells/dacryocytes; cloud-like megakaryocytes; serum type-III procollagen peptide increased; aspirate dry tap; biopsy silver impregnation reticulin ± collagen fibrosis with hypercellular marrow; note megakaryocytes in peripheral smear.
Megakaryocyte glossary: staghorn ET, giant ITP, cloud-like PMF, dwarf CML.
Median survival 5 years; medical oral ruxolitinib (JAK-2) and lenalidomide; definitive AHSCT limited by complete-match requirement and ↑ infection risk.

units.title: Essential Thrombocytosis: Etiology, Clinical Features, Investigations and Complications
units.sec: Essential Thrombocytosis: Etiology, Clinical Features, Investigations and Complications
units.guide:
Benign disease, good prognosis; JAK-2 50–60%, CALR 30–40%, MPL 10–20%; mild splenomegaly; thrombosis (hyperplasia) > bleeding (dysplastic cells); female > male.
RBC/WBC normal, PLC >4.5 lakhs; biopsy megakaryocyte hyperplasia (few dysplastic) with staghorn cells (giant, mature cytoplasm, hyperlobulated nuclei); photos: ↑ megakaryocytes, hyperlobulated nuclei, megakaryocyte in aspirate.
Least conversion to myelofibrosis; AML order PCRV > PMF > ET.

units.title: Essential Thrombocytosis: Evaluation and Risk-Stratified Management
units.sec: Essential Thrombocytosis: Evaluation and Risk-Stratified Management
units.guide:
Diagnosis by exclusion: rule out reactive thrombocytosis (normal RBC/WBC, response to inflammation) and other MPN/MDS (JAK-2, calreticulin, MPL).
Low risk <60 yrs: aspirin 75 mg/day; high risk (>60 yrs, h/o thrombosis, platelets >1.5 × 10⁶): aspirin + hydroxyurea > interferon > anagrelide.
